title: The square root of a complex number

board_content.text: Set $\sqrt{a+ib}=x+iy$, square, and equate real and imaginary parts.
Then fix the sign so that the sign of $xy$ matches the sign of $b$.
There are always TWO square roots, $\pm(x+iy)$.
This is what makes the quadratic formula usable even when $D$ is complex.

segments_english.text: To handle quadratics with complex discriminants, we need one more tool: the square root of a complex number, found directly.
The method is Method B in disguise. Set root of a plus i b equal to x plus i y, square both sides, and equate real and imaginary parts.
Squaring x plus i y gives x squared minus y squared plus two i x y. Matching parts: x squared minus y squared equals a, and two x y equals b.
Combined with the modulus, these solve neatly: x squared is the modulus plus a, over two, and y squared is the modulus minus a, over two, where the modulus is root of a squared plus b squared.
That gives the sizes of x and y, but you still must fix their signs. The rule is: choose signs so that the sign of the product x y matches the sign of b.
And there are always exactly two square roots, plus or minus the whole thing x plus i y, just as every positive real has two square roots.
This is precisely the tool that makes the quadratic formula work even when the discriminant itself is complex — you can now take the root of any complex number.
For example, root of three plus four i. The modulus is five, so x squared is four and y squared is one. Since b is positive, x y is positive, giving plus or minus two plus i.

segments_hinglish.text: Complex discriminants wali quadratics handle karne ke liye, humein ek aur tool chahiye: complex number ka square root, seedha nikaala hua.
Method Method B ka bhes badla roop hai. Root of a plus i b ko x plus i y ke barabar set karo, dono taraf square karo, aur real aur imaginary parts equate karo.
x plus i y ko square karne se milta hai x squared minus y squared plus two i x y. Parts match karo: x squared minus y squared barabar a, aur two x y barabar b.
Modulus ke saath, ye neatly solve hote hain: x squared hai modulus plus a, over two, aur y squared hai modulus minus a, over two, jahan modulus hai a squared plus b squared ka root.
Ye x aur y ke sizes deta hai, par aapko abhi unke signs fix karne hain. Rule hai: signs aise chuno ki product x y ka sign b ke sign se match kare.
Aur hamesha theek do square roots hote hain, plus or minus poora x plus i y, bilkul jaise har positive real ke do square roots hote hain.
Ye bilkul wahi tool hai jo quadratic formula ko tab bhi kaam karwaata hai jab discriminant khud complex ho — aap ab kisi bhi complex number ka root le sakte ho.
Misaal ke liye, root of three plus four i. Modulus hai five, to x squared hai four aur y squared hai one. Kyunki b positive hai, x y positive hai, deta hai plus or minus two plus i.
